report.title: Red Lions win 3-2 after extra-time swing
report.summary: Red Lions beat Blue Sharks 3-2 after extra time in a match that moved through five goals: Fox scored in the 28th minute, Gray equalised in the 62nd, Reid put Red Lions back ahead in the 95th, Cruz levelled again in the 105th, and Bell’s own goal in the 113th made it 3-2. Red Lions finished with stronger overall territory, possession, passing volume and chance production, while the final 10 minutes were marked by heavy Red Lions control but a chaotic rhythm.

sections.text: Red Lions won 3-2 after extra time in a match that swung back and forth all the way through. Fox scored in the 28th minute, Gray equalised in the 62nd, Reid restored Red Lions’ lead in the 95th, Cruz made it 2-2 in the 105th, and Bell’s own goal in the 113th put Red Lions back in front. It was a wild finish, with the scoreline changing again and again under pressure.

Red Lions finished with 4.61 expected goals to 2.48, 27 shots to 15, 11 shots on target to 7, and 6 big chances to 5. Red Lions also completed 776 of 838 passes at 93 percent accuracy, compared with Blue Sharks' 321 of 376 at 85 percent, and held 85 percent of final-third actions and 69 percent of possession overall. In the last 10 minutes, Red Lions had 91 percent of final-third actions and 79 percent of possession, with the match state described as chaotic.

Red Lions won 3-2 after extra time. Fox gave Red Lions the lead in the 28th minute, Gray levelled for Blue Sharks in the 62nd, Reid restored the lead in the 95th, Cruz made it 2-2 in the 105th, and Bell’s own goal in the 113th ended the scoring at 3-2. Red Lions controlled most of the game and especially the closing stages, with strong territory, possession and passing numbers.

fan.title: Red Lions edge wild extra-time battle
paragraphs: Red Lions came out on top 3-2 after extra time in a match that swung wildly from start to finish. Fox put Red Lions ahead in the 28th minute, Gray levelled for Blue Sharks in the 62nd, and Reid restored the lead in the 95th before Cruz brought it back to 2-2 in the 105th. The final strike came in the 113th minute, when Bell put the ball into the Blue Sharks net for the goal that settled the contest.

Red Lions controlled most of the game, especially through the ball, with 69 possession, 85 field tilt and 110 entries into the final third. Blue Sharks had spells of danger and created five big chances, but Red Lions produced more overall threat with 27 shots and six big chances, while Blue Sharks managed 15 shots and five big chances.

The turning point was the pressure after Red Lions’ 95th-minute goal, when Blue Sharks still found a reply but could not withstand the home side’s constant territory late on. Red Lions stayed on the front foot right to the end, and Bell’s effort in extra time finally made the difference.

analyst.title: Red Lions survive extra-time chaos to edge Blue Sharks 3-2
paragraphs: Red Lions took control for long stretches and finished with far more of the ball, more territory, and much more passing volume, completing 776 of 838 passes with 93 percent accuracy. That dominance showed in the numbers and the chance count: 27 shots, 11 on target, and 6 big chances, compared with Blue Sharks' 15 shots, 7 on target, and 5 big chances. The match stayed open throughout, though, and Blue Sharks kept finding answers.

Fox put Red Lions ahead in the 28th minute from Lane's assist, Gray levelled for Blue Sharks in the 62nd from Frost's pass, and Reid restored Red Lions' lead in the 95th minute after Rook set it up. Cruz dragged Blue Sharks back level in the 105th minute from Wells' assist, before Bell's own goal in the 113th minute put Red Lions back in front. The turning point was Red Lions' ability to keep pressing in extra time, especially in the last 10 minutes when they had 91 percent of final-third actions and 79 percent of possession, even though that spell was chaotic rather than calm.
